failure_modes: Reproducible co-isolation artefact: a process-consistent non-vesicular particle (protein aggregate, lipoprotein, or reagent-associated complex) that is detergent-insensitive or partially detergent-sensitive could carry the targeted miRNAs/proteins and pass the protection assays, producing false attribution to EVs (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Assay cross-reactivity or buffer interference: capture reagents, eluants, or spike-ins could produce matrix effects or reagent-bound signals that mimic protected cargo despite spike-in controls, yielding false positives.

Insufficient analytical sensitivity or recovery variability: low abundance true EV cargo falls below detection in some lots leading to false negatives, or spike-in tracer does not mimic endogenous cargo behavior, invalidating recovery normalization (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Panel-selection misspecification (Type II error): chosen miRNA/protein panel does not include conserved, biologically relevant cargo, so lots with correct EV content are falsely rejected because the panel misses the true markers (ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus indicating variability across models and sources).

Capture-reagent bias: immuno-capture against selected markers (CD63/CD9/CD81 or alternatives) could enrich a subpopulation that is not representative of therapeutic EVs or could preferentially bind non-EV complexes, producing a non-generalizable fingerprint (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Process-driven variability masquerading as biological signal: differences in TFF/SEC/iodixanol handling or donor/source heterogeneity could create lot-to-lot differences that the fingerprint reflects, confounding interpretation of whether variability is biological or manufacturing-related (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Lack of linkage to functional delivery/potency or to relevant in vivo biodistribution: even if the fingerprint genuinely marks membrane-protected cargo, it may not correlate with bioavailability or efficacy in relevant species/routes (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome).

Poor cross-species or route generalizability: protected cargo observed in mouse models or in vitro may not predict behavior in larger animals or humans (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome vs ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).
strongest_objection: The single strongest, bounded failure mode is that the observed “protected-cargo fingerprint” simply tracks a co-isolated, detergent-resistant or otherwise assay-reactive non-vesicular complex (or a capture-reagent–dependent artefact) that is reproducibly produced by the process, so the fingerprint would be reproducible across lots yet not report bona fide membrane-protected EV cargo nor predict in vivo delivery or potency. This outcome is consistent with ISEV concerns about co-isolates and assay specificity and with non-human-primate intranasal biodistribution data showing negligible brain delivery despite measurable, process-retained signal in lavage, so a reproducible fingerprint could be misleading for translational or CMC decisions.
